name: Fibula
description: Proximal fibula: head, styloid apex, neck and shaft, meeting the posterolateral tibial condyle at the proximal tibiofibular joint. The LCL and biceps insert on the lateral head, the popliteofibular, arcuate and fabellofibular ligaments on the styloid, and the common fibular (peroneal) nerve winds around the neck.
variants_pitfalls: Arcuate sign: a small horizontal flake or isolated marrow edema at the styloid marks a posterolateral corner injury; in one series all 13 patients also had a PCL injury. A rounded corticated ossicle behind the lateral femoral condyle is the fabella.

The proximal tibiofibular joint communicates with the knee in a reported 10–64%. Its fluid can track along the articular branch into the common fibular nerve as an intraneural ganglion: look for a tubular cyst along the nerve at the fibular neck and denervation edema in the anterior and lateral compartments.
Joint shape (horizontal under 20°, oblique over 20°) is a variant; most subluxations in the original series were oblique, but shape alone is not instability.
